tools.name: Monitor
tools.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

tools.name: PushNotification
tools.description:
This tool sends a desktop notification in the user's terminal. If Remote Control is connected, it also pushes to their phone. Either way, it pulls their attention from whatever they're doing — a meeting, another task, dinner — to this session. That's the cost. The benefit is they learn something now that they'd want to know now: a long task finished while they were away, a build is ready, you've hit something that needs their decision before you can continue.

Because a notification they didn't need is annoying in a way that accumulates, err toward not sending one. Don't notify for routine progress, or to announce you've answered something they asked seconds ago and are clearly still watching, or when a quick task completes. Notify when there's a real chance they've walked away and there's something worth coming back for — or when they've explicitly asked you to notify them.

Keep the message under 200 characters, one line, no markdown. Lead with what they'd act on — "build failed: 2 auth tests" tells them more than "task done" and more than a status dump.

When the user is actively at the terminal, your output already reaches them — a notification on top of it would be a duplicate, so the tool skips it and says so. A "not sent" result is expected and only ever about this one notification: it was redundant, turned off, or had nowhere to go.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendMessage
tools.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

1	# Plan: Database-Driven Dynamic Scope System (Refactor)
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	Current scoped access is `Dictionary<string, IReadOnlyCollection<string>>` stored as a single Keycloak user attribute `iam.scoped_access` (JSON) and surfaced as `iam_access` claim. It already supports dynamic keys but is **unvalidated, ungoverned, and opaque**:
6	
7	- Deserialization fails on `"test-key": "items-1"` vs `"test-key": ["items-1"]` because `RawAssignment.Scopes` is `Dictionary<string,string[]>` and the serializer has no scalar-to-array converter — raw `JsonException` leaks via default ASP.NET error handling.
8	- No registry of valid scope keys; any string is accepted. No `IsActive` / `ValueType`.
9	- No restriction on which scopes apply to which resources — `region` could filter any entity if business code wires it.
10	- User scopes are an opaque JSON blob in Keycloak user attributes, not normalized/queryable in SQL, not indexed, hard to audit/migrate.
11	- Authorization primitives (`ICurrentAccessContext`, `CurrentAccessContext`, `ClaimsPrincipalAccessContext`) are claims-only or Keycloak-attribute-backed, not resource-aware (`CanUseScope(resource)`).
12	- Query filtering is ad-hoc (`allowed.Contains(x.Region)` in sample) — no reusable, safe, type-safe `scopeFilter.Apply(query, currentUser, Resource)` abstraction. Risk of building raw SQL / reflection over client-supplied property names.
13	- Validation/errors return raw exceptions instead of field-level `ProblemDetails`.
14	
15	The request is a **full refactor** (19 deliverables): dynamic DTO, DB-driven scope registry, scope→resource mapping, safe filter handlers, normalized user-scope persistence, centralized current-user context, reusable EF Core filtering, cross-resource abuse prevention, role↔scope restrictions, value validation, resource registry, clean errors, security/performance, migrations/seeds, admin APIs, backward compat, and 18 test scenarios.
16	
17	Preserve: existing permission-sync flow (`RequirePermission` → `InMemoryPermissionRegistry` → `KeycloakSyncingPermissionRegistry`), `Company.Identity.Authorization` policy provider, Scalar/OpenAPI single `v1` doc, Options pattern, `TreatWarningsAsErrors`, no hard-coded realm/URLs.
18	
19	---
20	
21	## Diagnosis (current deserialization bug)
22	
23	`ScopedAccessDtos.cs: ScopedRoleAssignmentDto.Scopes` is `IReadOnlyDictionary<string,IReadOnlyCollection<string>>` but `ScopedAccessSerializer.RawAssignment.Scopes` is `Dictionary<string,string[]>`. `System.Text.Json` requires the JSON value to be an array for `string[]`; a bare string `"items-1"` fails before `Validate()` runs. `Program.cs` registers default `JsonOptions` (no custom converter, no `ProblemDetails` mapping), so the exception surfaces as `JsonException: Path $.assignments[0].scopes.test-key` instead of a field error.
24	
25	Fix alone is a `JsonConverter<IReadOnlyDictionary<string,IReadOnlyCollection<string>>>` that accepts `string | string[]` and normalizes to `string[]`. The plan keeps that converter but makes it the **smallest piece** of a larger validated model.
26	
27	---
28	
29	## Target Architecture
30	
31	### Separation of concerns
32	
33	```
34	ScopeDefinition          What scope types exist? (DB, admin-managed)
35	RoleAllowedScope         Which scopes may a role receive? (DB)
36	ApplicationResource      Which domain resources exist? (code registry + optional DB mirror)
37	ScopeResourceMapping     Which scopes may filter which resources? (DB)
38	ScopeFilterHandler       How does (scope, resource) filter translate to EF predicate? (code, type-safe)
39	User scopes              Which values were assigned? (normalized DB tables, queryable)
40	Current User Context     Effective scopes for the caller (claims + DB, cache, resource-aware)
41	ScopeFilter.Apply        One call to apply all applicable scope predicates to an IQueryable<T>
42	```
43	
44	Adding a new scope = 1) seed `ScopeDefinition` 2) configure `RoleAllowedScope` if needed 3) configure `ScopeResourceMapping` 4) register `IScopeValueValidator` (optional) 5) register `IScopeFilterHandler<TResource>` for each resource it may affect. No DTO property added.
45	
46	### Key decisions
47	
48	| Decision | Choice | Why |
49	|---|---|---|
50	| **Source of truth for user scopes** | **DB** (new tables in KeyMetadata DB / dedicated `IdentityScopeDbContext` sharing same connection string). Keycloak `iam.scoped_access` attribute deprecated, kept as read-through during migration then removed. Claim `iam_access` still emitted but now assembled from DB via facade, not from user attribute mapper. | Meets "persist normalized and queryable" and validation requirements. Keeps Keycloak for users/roles/permissions (existing boundary) but scopes become governable. Alternate of staying on Keycloak attribute cannot satisfy unique constraints, FKs, indexes, value validation, or resource mapping without a second store anyway. |
51	| **Where to host the new tables** | Extend existing `KeyMetadataDbContext` **or** add `ScopeDbContext` in a new project `Identity.Persistence.Scopes` that reuses the same connection string (`ConnectionStrings:KeyMetadata` / `Identity:KeyMetadata`). Prefer a **new DbContext** to avoid coupling key-rotation schema, but share the same physical DB (SQLite/Postgres/Oracle) and provider switch. Reuse `ConfigureProvider`. | Keeps migrations focused; no new physical DB. Fits existing provider abstraction and `AddDbContext` pattern in `Program.cs`. |
52	| **DTO scalar support** | Support it: single custom converter `ScopeDictionaryConverter : JsonConverter<IReadOnlyDictionary<string,IReadOnlyCollection<string>>>` that reads `JsonValueKind.String` as single-item array, `Array` as array, otherwise fails with a clean message. Internally always `IReadOnlyCollection<string>`. | Matches user expectation and avoids breaking existing callers that already send arrays. Converter lives in `Identity.Contracts` (or `Identity.Application`) and is registered via `JsonOptions` globally + on the DTO property via `[JsonConverter]`. |
53	| **Filter safety** | **Registry of strongly typed handlers**. `IScopeFilterHandler<TResource>` or non-generic `IScopeFilterHandler { string ResourceKey; string ScopeKey; IQueryable<T> Apply(...) }` registered in DI. `ScopeFilterService.ApplyAsync<T>(IQueryable<T> query, ICurrentScopeContext ctx, string resourceKey)` looks up allowed scopes for the resource from DB/cache, intersects with user's scopes, and invokes only registered handlers. No `EF.Property` with client-supplied name, no string-concatenated SQL, always parameterized `Contains` / `IN`. | Database decides *which* filter applies; code decides *how*. Prevents injection and cross-resource abuse. |
54	| **Resource registry** | Code constants `ResourceKeys` / `ApplicationResourceDescriptor` registry (`IApplicationResourceRegistry`) plus optional DB mirror `ApplicationResource` table seeded from code at startup. API validates `resourceKey` against registry; unknown resource => deny (empty result or 403, never unrestricted). | Avoids exposing physical table names; keeps `Orders`, `ProjectTasks`, etc. as stable keys. |
55	| **Caching** | `IMemoryCache` (or `HybridCache` if available) for `Active ScopeDefinitions + ScopeResourceMappings + RoleAllowedScopes + ResourceDescriptors`. User-specific scopes are per-request from DB/claims, not cached globally (or cached per-user with short TTL + invalidation on assignment change). Invalidation via `IScopeCacheInvalidator` called from admin/management endpoints. | Avoids per-entity DB round trips. Consistent with existing "no distributed cache unless needed". |
56	| **Claims vs DB at request time** | Keep `ICurrentAccessContext.EnsureLoadedAsync` (facade fallback) but change facade's `GET /api/identity/access-context` to read from DB. For microservices: token carries only `sub`/`permissions` (and optionally a compact `scp_version` / small `iam_access` for perf); `EnsureLoadedAsync` populates scopes from facade on first use. Alternative of stuffing all scopes into JWT is bounded by `MaxInlineClaimBytes` and now unnecessary since DB is authoritative — prefer claim-light. | Prevents large tokens while keeping local authz fast. |
57	
58	---
59	
60	## Data & Entity Model
61	
62	### New EF entities (in `Identity.Persistence.Scopes` or extended `KeyMetadataDbContext`)
63	
64	```csharp
65	ScopeDefinition { Guid Id PK, string Key Unique CI (e.g. "region"), string DisplayName, string? Description,
66	                  bool IsActive, string ValueType (enum string: String/Guid/Int), DateTimeOffset CreatedAt, UpdatedAt,
67	                  // unicase index on Key, filtered index on IsActive }
68	ApplicationResource { Guid Id PK, string Key Unique (e.g. "Orders"), string DisplayName, string? Description }
69	ScopeResourceMapping { Guid ScopeDefinitionId FK -> ScopeDefinition, Guid ApplicationResourceId FK -> ApplicationResource,
70	                       PK = (ScopeDefinitionId, ApplicationResourceId) }
71	RoleAllowedScope { string RoleName (or FK to business role if roles become DB-backed — currently roles are Keycloak composite realm roles, so store RoleName string + optional RoleId), Guid ScopeDefinitionId FK, PK=(RoleName,ScopeDefinitionId) }
72	UserRoleAssignment { Guid Id PK, string UserId (Keycloak user id, indexed), string RoleName, DateTimeOffset AssignedAt,
73	                     Unique(UserId, RoleName) }
74	AssignmentScope { Guid Id PK, Guid UserRoleAssignmentId FK, Guid ScopeDefinitionId FK, Unique(AssignmentId, ScopeDefinitionId) }
75	AssignmentScopeValue { Guid Id PK, Guid AssignmentScopeId FK, string Value (max 256), Index(AssignmentScopeId, Value) }
76	```
77	
78	- All string keys normalized (trim, case per spec: treat scope keys case-sensitive `Ordinal`, store lower or as-provided but enforce uniqueness `OrdinalIgnoreCase` or `Ordinal` — decide and document; recommend `OrdinalIgnoreCase` uniqueness with normalized lower storage).
79	- FKs with cascade delete from `UserRoleAssignment` → `AssignmentScope` → `AssignmentScopeValue`.
80	- Alternate simplified model `UserScopeValue { UserId, RoleName, ScopeDefinitionId, Value }` is acceptable if it preserves queryability; pick one and keep assignment grouping so `GetScopeValues` unions across roles.
81	
82	### Seed data
83	
84	Migrate existing built-in scopes: `region`, `branch` + new examples `department`, `organization`, `warehouse`, `customer`, `project`, `test-key` (as requested). Map:
85	- `region -> Orders, Branches, Employees`
86	- `branch -> Orders, Employees`
87	- `project -> ProjectTasks, ProjectDocuments`
88	- `test-key -> ResourceA` (or `TestResource` placeholder used in tests)
89	Seed `ApplicationResource` for `Orders`, `Branches`, `Employees`, `ProjectTasks`, `ProjectDocuments`, `CustomerOrders`, `ResourceA`, etc.
90	
91	Provide an EF migration that preserves existing user scope data: if any `iam.scoped_access` attributes exist, a one-time startup migrator reads them via `KeycloakScopedAccessStore` and writes normalized rows.
92	
93	---
94	
95	## DTO / Validation Changes
96	
97	- Keep `ScopedRoleAssignmentDto.Scopes: IReadOnlyDictionary<string,IReadOnlyCollection<string>>` but annotate with `[JsonConverter(typeof(ScopeDictionaryConverter))]` and normalize scalar → array.
98	- Add `ScopeDictionaryConverter` that on `Read`: iterates properties, accepts `String` or `Array` of strings, trims, de-dupes, rejects other kinds with `JsonException` that is translated to `ValidationProblemDetails` by a new exception filter (`JsonExceptionFilter` or `AddControllers().AddJsonOptions` + `InvalidModelStateResponseFactory`).
99	- Validation pipeline (in `ProvisioningOrchestrator` + new `ScopeAssignmentValidator`):
100	  1) role exists (`IBusinessRoleStore.GetAsync`)
101	  2) each scope key exists && `IsActive`
102	  3) `RoleAllowedScope` allows it (if any rows for the role; if none, allow all active scopes — decide policy and document; recommend "restrictive if configured, permissive otherwise" or always require explicit mapping — pick restrictive for security and seed mappings accordingly)
103	  4) value non-empty, length, optional `IScopeValueValidator` per scope (registry `IScopeValueValidatorProvider.GetValidator(scopeKey)`; default `NonEmptyStringValidator`; `RegionExistsValidator` etc. can be registered without switch).
104	- Return field-level errors: `ValidationProblemDetails` with keys like `assignments[0].scopes.test-key` or `assignments[0].scopes.unknown-scope`.
105	
106	---
107	
108	## Service & Abstractions
109	
110	- `IScopeDefinitionService` — CRUD + `ListActiveAsync`, `GetByKeyAsync`, cache.
111	- `IScopeResourceMappingService` — `GetResourcesForScopeAsync`, `GetScopesForResourceAsync`.
112	- `IRoleScopeService` — `IsScopeAllowedForRoleAsync`, `GetAllowedScopesForRoleAsync`.
113	- `IScopeValueValidator` / `IScopeValueValidatorRegistry` — extensible.
114	- `IApplicationResourceRegistry` — code registry of `ResourceDescriptor { Key, ClrType, DisplayName }`.
115	- `IScopeFilterRegistry` / `IScopeFilterHandler<T>` — DI-registered handlers; `ScopeFilterService : IScopeFilterService` with `IQueryable<T> Apply<T>(IQueryable<T> query, ICurrentScopeContext ctx, string resourceKey)`.
116	- `ICurrentScopeContext` (extends `ICurrentAccessContext`) — `bool HasScope(key)`, `IReadOnlyCollection<string> GetScopeValues(key)`, `bool HasScopeValue(key,val)`, `bool CanUseScope(key, resourceKey)`, `Task EnsureLoadedAsync`. Implementation `DbBackedAccessContext` reads from DB via `IUserScopeReader`; caches per-request.
117	- `IUserScopeReader` / `IUserScopeWriter` — DB persistence for assignments/scopes/values.
118	
119	---
120	
121	## Query Filtering Semantics (document & test)
122	
123	- Within one scope: values combined with **OR** (`IN` / `Contains`) — user with `region: [tehran-1, tehran-2]` matches `Region IN (...)`.
124	- Across different scopes for the same resource: **AND** — `region IN (...) AND branch IN (...)`. Only scopes mapped to the resource participate; unmapped scopes are ignored for that resource (and `CanUseScope` returns false).
125	- No applicable scopes for a resource + user has no scopes for that resource => **deny by default** (return empty query `Where(_ => false)`), not unrestricted. Policy configurable per resource (`RequireScope` vs `AllowUnscoped`) but default is deny.
126	- All predicates are parameterized; no raw SQL.
127	
128	---
129

# Plan: Database-Driven Dynamic Scope System (Refactor)

## Context

Current scoped access is `Dictionary<string, IReadOnlyCollection<string>>` stored as a single Keycloak user attribute `iam.scoped_access` (JSON) and surfaced as `iam_access` claim. It already supports dynamic keys but is **unvalidated, ungoverned, and opaque**:

- Deserialization fails on `"test-key": "items-1"` vs `"test-key": ["items-1"]` because `RawAssignment.Scopes` is `Dictionary<string,string[]>` and the serializer has no scalar-to-array converter — raw `JsonException` leaks via default ASP.NET error handling.
- No registry of valid scope keys; any string is accepted. No `IsActive` / `ValueType`.
- No restriction on which scopes apply to which resources — `region` could filter any entity if business code wires it.
- User scopes are an opaque JSON blob in Keycloak user attributes, not normalized/queryable in SQL, not indexed, hard to audit/migrate.
- Authorization primitives (`ICurrentAccessContext`, `CurrentAccessContext`, `ClaimsPrincipalAccessContext`) are claims-only or Keycloak-attribute-backed, not resource-aware (`CanUseScope(resource)`).
- Query filtering is ad-hoc (`allowed.Contains(x.Region)` in sample) — no reusable, safe, type-safe `scopeFilter.Apply(query, currentUser, Resource)` abstraction. Risk of building raw SQL / reflection over client-supplied property names.
- Validation/errors return raw exceptions instead of field-level `ProblemDetails`.

The request is a **full refactor** (19 deliverables): dynamic DTO, DB-driven scope registry, scope→resource mapping, safe filter handlers, normalized user-scope persistence, centralized current-user context, reusable EF Core filtering, cross-resource abuse prevention, role↔scope restrictions, value validation, resource registry, clean errors, security/performance, migrations/seeds, admin APIs, backward compat, and 18 test scenarios.

Preserve: existing permission-sync flow (`RequirePermission` → `InMemoryPermissionRegistry` → `KeycloakSyncingPermissionRegistry`), `Company.Identity.Authorization` policy provider, Scalar/OpenAPI single `v1` doc, Options pattern, `TreatWarningsAsErrors`, no hard-coded realm/URLs.

---

## Diagnosis (current deserialization bug)

`ScopedAccessDtos.cs: ScopedRoleAssignmentDto.Scopes` is `IReadOnlyDictionary<string,IReadOnlyCollection<string>>` but `ScopedAccessSerializer.RawAssignment.Scopes` is `Dictionary<string,string[]>`. `System.Text.Json` requires the JSON value to be an array for `string[]`; a bare string `"items-1"` fails before `Validate()` runs. `Program.cs` registers default `JsonOptions` (no custom converter, no `ProblemDetails` mapping), so the exception surfaces as `JsonException: Path $.assignments[0].scopes.test-key` instead of a field error.

Fix alone is a `JsonConverter<IReadOnlyDictionary<string,IReadOnlyCollection<string>>>` that accepts `string | string[]` and normalizes to `string[]`. The plan keeps that converter but makes it the **smallest piece** of a larger validated model.

---

## Target Architecture

### Separation of concerns

```
ScopeDefinition          What scope types exist? (DB, admin-managed)
RoleAllowedScope         Which scopes may a role receive? (DB)
ApplicationResource      Which domain resources exist? (code registry + optional DB mirror)
ScopeResourceMapping     Which scopes may filter which resources? (DB)
ScopeFilterHandler       How does (scope, resource) filter translate to EF predicate? (code, type-safe)
User scopes              Which values were assigned? (normalized DB tables, queryable)
Current User Context     Effective scopes for the caller (claims + DB, cache, resource-aware)
ScopeFilter.Apply        One call to apply all applicable scope predicates to an IQueryable<T>
```

Adding a new scope = 1) seed `ScopeDefinition` 2) configure `RoleAllowedScope` if needed 3) configure `ScopeResourceMapping` 4) register `IScopeValueValidator` (optional) 5) register `IScopeFilterHandler<TResource>` for each resource it may affect. No DTO property added.

### Key decisions

| Decision | Choice | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Source of truth for user scopes** | **DB** (new tables in KeyMetadata DB / dedicated `IdentityScopeDbContext` sharing same connection string). Keycloak `iam.scoped_access` attribute deprecated, kept as read-through during migration then removed. Claim `iam_access` still emitted but now assembled from DB via facade, not from user attribute mapper. | Meets "persist normalized and queryable" and validation requirements. Keeps Keycloak for users/roles/permissions (existing boundary) but scopes become governable. Alternate of staying on Keycloak attribute cannot satisfy unique constraints, FKs, indexes, value validation, or resource mapping without a second store anyway. |
| **Where to host the new tables** | Extend existing `KeyMetadataDbContext` **or** add `ScopeDbContext` in a new project `Identity.Persistence.Scopes` that reuses the same connection string (`ConnectionStrings:KeyMetadata` / `Identity:KeyMetadata`). Prefer a **new DbContext** to avoid coupling key-rotation schema, but share the same physical DB (SQLite/Postgres/Oracle) and provider switch. Reuse `ConfigureProvider`. | Keeps migrations focused; no new physical DB. Fits existing provider abstraction and `AddDbContext` pattern in `Program.cs`. |
| **DTO scalar support** | Support it: single custom converter `ScopeDictionaryConverter : JsonConverter<IReadOnlyDictionary<string,IReadOnlyCollection<string>>>` that reads `JsonValueKind.String` as single-item array, `Array` as array, otherwise fails with a clean message. Internally always `IReadOnlyCollection<string>`. | Matches user expectation and avoids breaking existing callers that already send arrays. Converter lives in `Identity.Contracts` (or `Identity.Application`) and is registered via `JsonOptions` globally + on the DTO property via `[JsonConverter]`. |
| **Filter safety** | **Registry of strongly typed handlers**. `IScopeFilterHandler<TResource>` or non-generic `IScopeFilterHandler { string ResourceKey; string ScopeKey; IQueryable<T> Apply(...) }` registered in DI. `ScopeFilterService.ApplyAsync<T>(IQueryable<T> query, ICurrentScopeContext ctx, string resourceKey)` looks up allowed scopes for the resource from DB/cache, intersects with user's scopes, and invokes only registered handlers. No `EF.Property` with client-supplied name, no string-concatenated SQL, always parameterized `Contains` / `IN`. | Database decides *which* filter applies; code decides *how*. Prevents injection and cross-resource abuse. |
| **Resource registry** | Code constants `ResourceKeys` / `ApplicationResourceDescriptor` registry (`IApplicationResourceRegistry`) plus optional DB mirror `ApplicationResource` table seeded from code at startup. API validates `resourceKey` against registry; unknown resource => deny (empty result or 403, never unrestricted). | Avoids exposing physical table names; keeps `Orders`, `ProjectTasks`, etc. as stable keys. |
| **Caching** | `IMemoryCache` (or `HybridCache` if available) for `Active ScopeDefinitions + ScopeResourceMappings + RoleAllowedScopes + ResourceDescriptors`. User-specific scopes are per-request from DB/claims, not cached globally (or cached per-user with short TTL + invalidation on assignment change). Invalidation via `IScopeCacheInvalidator` called from admin/management endpoints. | Avoids per-entity DB round trips. Consistent with existing "no distributed cache unless needed". |
| **Claims vs DB at request time** | Keep `ICurrentAccessContext.EnsureLoadedAsync` (facade fallback) but change facade's `GET /api/identity/access-context` to read from DB. For microservices: token carries only `sub`/`permissions` (and optionally a compact `scp_version` / small `iam_access` for perf); `EnsureLoadedAsync` populates scopes from facade on first use. Alternative of stuffing all scopes into JWT is bounded by `MaxInlineClaimBytes` and now unnecessary since DB is authoritative — prefer claim-light. | Prevents large tokens while keeping local authz fast. |

---

## Data & Entity Model

### New EF entities (in `Identity.Persistence.Scopes` or extended `KeyMetadataDbContext`)

```csharp
ScopeDefinition { Guid Id PK, string Key Unique CI (e.g. "region"), string DisplayName, string? Description,
                  bool IsActive, string ValueType (enum string: String/Guid/Int), DateTimeOffset CreatedAt, UpdatedAt,
                  // unicase index on Key, filtered index on IsActive }
ApplicationResource { Guid Id PK, string Key Unique (e.g. "Orders"), string DisplayName, string? Description }
ScopeResourceMapping { Guid ScopeDefinitionId FK -> ScopeDefinition, Guid ApplicationResourceId FK -> ApplicationResource,
                       PK = (ScopeDefinitionId, ApplicationResourceId) }
RoleAllowedScope { string RoleName (or FK to business role if roles become DB-backed — currently roles are Keycloak composite realm roles, so store RoleName string + optional RoleId), Guid ScopeDefinitionId FK, PK=(RoleName,ScopeDefinitionId) }
UserRoleAssignment { Guid Id PK, string UserId (Keycloak user id, indexed), string RoleName, DateTimeOffset AssignedAt,
                     Unique(UserId, RoleName) }
AssignmentScope { Guid Id PK, Guid UserRoleAssignmentId FK, Guid ScopeDefinitionId FK, Unique(AssignmentId, ScopeDefinitionId) }
AssignmentScopeValue { Guid Id PK, Guid AssignmentScopeId FK, string Value (max 256), Index(AssignmentScopeId, Value) }
```

- All string keys normalized (trim, case per spec: treat scope keys case-sensitive `Ordinal`, store lower or as-provided but enforce uniqueness `OrdinalIgnoreCase` or `Ordinal` — decide and document; recommend `OrdinalIgnoreCase` uniqueness with normalized lower storage).
- FKs with cascade delete from `UserRoleAssignment` → `AssignmentScope` → `AssignmentScopeValue`.
- Alternate simplified model `UserScopeValue { UserId, RoleName, ScopeDefinitionId, Value }` is acceptable if it preserves queryability; pick one and keep assignment grouping so `GetScopeValues` unions across roles.

### Seed data

Migrate existing built-in scopes: `region`, `branch` + new examples `department`, `organization`, `warehouse`, `customer`, `project`, `test-key` (as requested). Map:
- `region -> Orders, Branches, Employees`
- `branch -> Orders, Employees`
- `project -> ProjectTasks, ProjectDocuments`
- `test-key -> ResourceA` (or `TestResource` placeholder used in tests)
Seed `ApplicationResource` for `Orders`, `Branches`, `Employees`, `ProjectTasks`, `ProjectDocuments`, `CustomerOrders`, `ResourceA`, etc.

Provide an EF migration that preserves existing user scope data: if any `iam.scoped_access` attributes exist, a one-time startup migrator reads them via `KeycloakScopedAccessStore` and writes normalized rows.

---

## DTO / Validation Changes

- Keep `ScopedRoleAssignmentDto.Scopes: IReadOnlyDictionary<string,IReadOnlyCollection<string>>` but annotate with `[JsonConverter(typeof(ScopeDictionaryConverter))]` and normalize scalar → array.
- Add `ScopeDictionaryConverter` that on `Read`: iterates properties, accepts `String` or `Array` of strings, trims, de-dupes, rejects other kinds with `JsonException` that is translated to `ValidationProblemDetails` by a new exception filter (`JsonExceptionFilter` or `AddControllers().AddJsonOptions` + `InvalidModelStateResponseFactory`).
- Validation pipeline (in `ProvisioningOrchestrator` + new `ScopeAssignmentValidator`):
  1) role exists (`IBusinessRoleStore.GetAsync`)
  2) each scope key exists && `IsActive`
  3) `RoleAllowedScope` allows it (if any rows for the role; if none, allow all active scopes — decide policy and document; recommend "restrictive if configured, permissive otherwise" or always require explicit mapping — pick restrictive for security and seed mappings accordingly)
  4) value non-empty, length, optional `IScopeValueValidator` per scope (registry `IScopeValueValidatorProvider.GetValidator(scopeKey)`; default `NonEmptyStringValidator`; `RegionExistsValidator` etc. can be registered without switch).
- Return field-level errors: `ValidationProblemDetails` with keys like `assignments[0].scopes.test-key` or `assignments[0].scopes.unknown-scope`.

---

## Service & Abstractions

- `IScopeDefinitionService` — CRUD + `ListActiveAsync`, `GetByKeyAsync`, cache.
- `IScopeResourceMappingService` — `GetResourcesForScopeAsync`, `GetScopesForResourceAsync`.
- `IRoleScopeService` — `IsScopeAllowedForRoleAsync`, `GetAllowedScopesForRoleAsync`.
- `IScopeValueValidator` / `IScopeValueValidatorRegistry` — extensible.
- `IApplicationResourceRegistry` — code registry of `ResourceDescriptor { Key, ClrType, DisplayName }`.
- `IScopeFilterRegistry` / `IScopeFilterHandler<T>` — DI-registered handlers; `ScopeFilterService : IScopeFilterService` with `IQueryable<T> Apply<T>(IQueryable<T> query, ICurrentScopeContext ctx, string resourceKey)`.
- `ICurrentScopeContext` (extends `ICurrentAccessContext`) — `bool HasScope(key)`, `IReadOnlyCollection<string> GetScopeValues(key)`, `bool HasScopeValue(key,val)`, `bool CanUseScope(key, resourceKey)`, `Task EnsureLoadedAsync`. Implementation `DbBackedAccessContext` reads from DB via `IUserScopeReader`; caches per-request.
- `IUserScopeReader` / `IUserScopeWriter` — DB persistence for assignments/scopes/values.

---

## Query Filtering Semantics (document & test)

- Within one scope: values combined with **OR** (`IN` / `Contains`) — user with `region: [tehran-1, tehran-2]` matches `Region IN (...)`.
- Across different scopes for the same resource: **AND** — `region IN (...) AND branch IN (...)`. Only scopes mapped to the resource participate; unmapped scopes are ignored for that resource (and `CanUseScope` returns false).
- No applicable scopes for a resource + user has no scopes for that resource => **deny by default** (return empty query `Where(_ => false)`), not unrestricted. Policy configurable per resource (`RequireScope` vs `AllowUnscoped`) but default is deny.
- All predicates are parameterized; no raw SQL.

---

## Implementation Steps (ordered)

### Phase 1 — Converter + current DTO fix (no DB yet)
1. Add `ScopeDictionaryConverter` in `Identity.Contracts` (or `Identity.Application.Json`), register globally via `builder.Services.Configure<JsonOptions>` and annotate `ScopedRoleAssignmentDto.Scopes`.
2. Add `JsonException` → `ValidationProblemDetails` translation (middleware or `AddControllers` filter) so scalar/array mismatch returns field errors, not 500.
3. Unit tests: scalar `"test-key": "items-1"` normalizes, array still works, mixed array+empty ignored, invalid shape → 400.

### Phase 2 — Persistence model + migrations
4. Create project `Identity.Persistence.Scopes` (or extend `Identity.Persistence.KeyManagement`) — entities `ScopeDefinition`, `ApplicationResource`, `ScopeResourceMapping`, `RoleAllowedScope`, `UserRoleAssignment`, `AssignmentScope`, `AssignmentScopeValue` with EF configurations (unique, FK, indexes, max lengths).
5. Add `ScopeDbContext` with `ConfigureProvider` reuse; wire in `Program.cs` (`AddDbContext<ScopeDbContext>`).
6. Generate EF migration; add idempotent seed for `region`, `branch`, `department`, `project`, `customer`, `test-key`, resources and mappings; add startup migrator that copies any existing `iam.scoped_access` JSON into normalized rows (then optionally clears the Keycloak attribute).
7. Build + run migration locally (SQLite dev flow), verify tables.

### Phase 3 — Registry + validation + cache
8. Implement `ScopeDefinitionService`, `ScopeResourceService`, `RoleScopeService` with `IMemoryCache` and `IScopeCacheInvalidator`.
9. Implement `IScopeValueValidator` registry (default + per-scope validators, no switch).
10. Implement `ScopeAssignmentValidator` used by `ProvisioningOrchestrator` (role exists, scope exists/active, role-allowed, value validation).
11. Wire validation into `UserManagementEndpoints` and `ProvisioningOrchestrator` returning field-level `ValidationProblemDetails`.

### Phase 4 — Current-user context (resource-aware)
12. Replace/augment `ICurrentAccessContext` with resource-aware `ICurrentScopeContext` (keep old interface for compat, new methods `CanUseScope`, resource-aware `HasPermissionForResource`). Implementation `DbBackedCurrentScopeContext` loads scopes from DB via `IUserScopeReader` (or facade fallback for microservices).
13. Update `AccessContextEndpoints` (`GET /access-context`) to read from DB; keep `iam_access` claim emission from DB (size-guarded) for backward compat.

### Phase 5 — Safe EF Core filter pipeline
14. Define `IApplicationResourceRegistry` with constants `ResourceKeys.Orders`, `ResourceKeys.ProjectTasks`, etc., and register `IScopeFilterHandler<Order>` etc. (e.g., `RegionOrderFilter : IScopeFilterHandler<Order> { ScopeKey="region", ResourceKey="Orders", Apply = q => allowed => q.Where(o => allowed.Contains(o.RegionId)) }`).
15. Implement `ScopeFilterService.Apply<T>` that validates scope→resource mapping, intersects with user's scopes, invokes handlers, composes `AND` across scopes / `IN` within scope, denies by default when config missing.
16. Update `OrderService.Sample` to use `scopeFilter.Apply(db.Orders, currentUser, ResourceKeys.Orders)`.

### Phase 6 — Admin / management + docs + Scalar
17. Add endpoints: `GET /api/identity/scopes` (list), `GET /api/identity/scopes/{key}`, `GET /api/identity/scopes/{key}/resources`, `POST/PUT/PATCH /api/identity/scopes` (create/update/disable, guarded `identity.scopes.manage`), `GET /api/identity/users/{id}/scopes` view. Scalar auto-lists in `v1`.
18. Update `docs/architecture.md` + `docs/running.md` + `README.md` with new model and "add a new scope" guide (5 steps).
19. Update Postman collection with new scope-admin calls.

### Phase 7 — Tests & verification
20. Cover 18 scenarios: (1) valid dynamic scope, (2) multi-values, (3) multi-scopes, (4) unknown scope 400, (5) inactive 400, (6) invalid value 400, (7) role-not-allowed 400, (8) get effective scopes, (9) get individual values, (10) apply allowed resource, (11) prevent unrelated resource, (12) multi-values OR, (13) multi-dimensions AND, (14) no scope => deny not unrestricted, (15) malformed JSON clean error, (16) persistence reload, (17) update/removal, (18) after config change.
21. `dotnet build` / `dotnet test` (host SDK `/usr/share/dotnet`) — fix warnings.

---

## Files to Change

| Path | Action |
|---|---|
| `src/Identity.Contracts/ScopedAccessDtos.cs` | Add `[JsonConverter]` + keep `IReadOnlyDictionary` |
| `src/Identity.Contracts/ScopeDictionaryConverter.cs` | **New** — scalar/array normalizer |
| `src/Identity.Persistence.Scopes/**` (or `Identity.Persistence.KeyManagement`) | **New project or extension** — entities, configs, `ScopeDbContext`, migration, seeds, migrator |
| `src/Identity.Application/ScopeDefinitionService.cs`, `ScopeResourceService.cs`, `RoleScopeService.cs` | **New** |
| `src/Identity.Application/ScopeAssignmentValidator.cs`, `IScopeValueValidator.cs` | **New** |
| `src/Identity.Application/IUserScopeReader.cs`, `ScopeFilterService.cs`, `IScopeFilterHandler.cs` | **New** |
| `src/Identity.Application/ICurrentScopeContext.cs`, `DbBackedCurrentScopeContext.cs` | **New / replace** |
| `src/Company.Identity.Authorization/AccessContext.cs`, `FacadeResolvingAccessContext.cs` | **Modify** — resource-aware methods, DB fallback |
| `src/Identity.Api/Program.cs` | Wire `ScopeDbContext`, cache, filter registry, JSON options, exception filter |
| `src/Identity.Api/UserManagementEndpoints.cs`, `ProvisioningOrchestrator.cs` | **Modify** — use validator, normalized persistence, field errors |
| `src/Identity.Api/ScopeAdminEndpoints.cs` | **New** |
| `src/Identity.Infrastructure.Keycloak/KeycloakScopedAccessStore.cs` | **Modify or deprecate** — become migration source |
| `samples/OrderService.Sample/OrderService.cs`, `Program.cs` | **Modify** — demo `ScopeFilter.Apply` |
| `tests/Identity.Sample.Tests/**` | **Add** 18-scenario suite (unit + in-memory SQLite integration) |
| `docs/**`, `postman/**` | **Update** |
| `deploy/realm-company.json` | Keep (no new realm roles; scopes are DB) |

---

## Verification

2. `dotnet test` — all suites green including 18 new cases.
3. `GET /openapi/v1.json` contains `GET /api/identity/scopes` and new admin endpoints, all `security: [Bearer]` under single `v1`.
4. Manual: `POST /api/identity/users` with `"test-key": "items-1"` succeeds (converter); with `"test-key": ["items-1"]` also succeeds; with `"some-random-scope": ["123"]` → 400 field error `Scope 'some-random-scope' is not defined or is inactive.`; `GET /api/identity/users/{id}/scoped-access` returns normalized values; `ScopeFilter.Apply` on `Orders` with `test-key` (mapped only to `ResourceA`) does not affect `Orders` query.

Fixed. Root cause: `ScopeAssignmentValidator` was registered `Singleton` while depending on `IScopeDefinitionLookup` → `EfScopeDefinitionLookup` → `KeyMetadataDbContext` (`Scoped`). ASP.NET's scope validation fails the container at `WebApplicationBuilder.Build()`.

**Change:** [src/Identity.Api/Program.cs:73](src/Identity.Api/Program.cs#L73)

```diff
-builder.Services.AddSingleton<ScopeAssignmentValidator>();
+builder.Services.AddScoped<ScopeAssignmentValidator>();
```

`ScopeAssignmentValidator` is only consumed by `ProvisioningOrchestrator` (`Scoped`), so `Scoped` is correct — `IScopeValueValidatorRegistry` it depends on remains `Singleton` (stateless) which is allowed.

Verification: `dotnet build -v q` → `Build succeeded. 0 Warning(s) 0 Error(s)` (tests still green `63 Passed`).

**Next:**

```bash
cd deploy
docker compose up --build -d
docker compose ps   # identity-facade should be healthy now
docker compose logs identity-facade | tail -50
```

===
services:
  identity-facade:
    build:
      context: ..
      dockerfile: deploy/Identity.Api.Dockerfile
    environment:
      ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT: Development
      ASPNETCORE_URLS: http://+:5080
      Identity__Authority: http://keycloak:8080/realms/company
      # Keycloak proxy/admin base — the only place the facade's Keycloak address is configured.
      Identity__Keycloak__BaseUrl: http://keycloak:8080
      Identity__RequireHttpsMetadata: "false"
      Authentication__Schemes__Bearer__RequireHttpsMetadata: "false"
      # Public self-URL used to rewrite jwks_uri in the proxied discovery document.
      # Must match the host port published for the facade (FACADE_HTTP_PORT, default 5080).
      Identity__PublicBaseUrl: http://localhost:${FACADE_HTTP_PORT:-5080}
      # Tokens are minted for the facade's own Keycloak client, so its audience is that client id.
      Identity__Audience: identity-facade
      Identity__KeyMetadata__Provider: oracle
      ConnectionStrings__KeyMetadata: "User Id=identity_meta;Password=identity-development-only;Data Source=identity-meta-db:1521/XEPDB1"
      Identity__Vault__Address: http://vault:8200
      Identity__Vault__Token: root
      Identity__KeycloakAdmin__BaseUrl: http://keycloak:8080
      Identity__KeycloakAdmin__Realm: company
      # Admin bootstrap for KeycloakDirectoryAdapter / KeycloakKeyManager (dev only;
      # in prod replace with client-credentials via Identity__KeycloakAdmin__AdminClientSecret).
      Identity__KeycloakAdmin__AdminClientId: admin-cli
      Identity__KeycloakAdmin__AdminUsername: ${KEYCLOAK_ADMIN:-admin}
      Identity__KeycloakAdmin__AdminPassword: ${KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD:-admin-development-only}
      Identity__Redis__Configuration: redis:6379
    ports: [ "${FACADE_HTTP_PORT:-5080}:5080" ]
    healthcheck:
      # aspnet image ships no curl — probe over /dev/tcp.
      test: [ "CMD-SHELL", "bash -c 'exec 3<>/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/5080 && printf \"GET /health/live HTTP/1.1\\r\\nHost: localhost\\r\\nConnection: close\\r\\n\\r\\n\" >&3 && timeout 3 head -1 <&3 | grep -q 200'" ]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 12
      start_period: 30s
    depends_on:
      keycloak:
        condition: service_healthy
      identity-meta-db:
        condition: service_healthy
      vault:
        condition: service_started
      redis:
        condition: service_started

  keycloak:
    build:
      context: ..
      dockerfile: deploy/Keycloak.Dockerfile
    command: start-dev --http-port=8080 --import-realm
    environment:
      KC_DB: oracle
      KC_DB_URL: jdbc:oracle:thin:@keycloak-db:1521/XEPDB1
      KC_DB_USERNAME: keycloak
      KC_DB_PASSWORD: ${KEYCLOAK_DB_PASSWORD:-keycloak-development-only}
      KC_HEALTH_ENABLED: "true"
      KC_METRICS_ENABLED: "true"
      KC_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_USERNAME: ${KEYCLOAK_ADMIN:-admin}
      KC_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD: ${KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD:-admin-development-only}
    ports: [ "${KEYCLOAK_HTTP_PORT:-8080}:8080" ]
    volumes:
      - ./realm-company.json:/opt/keycloak/data/import/realm-company.json:ro
    depends_on:
      keycloak-db:
        condition: service_healthy
    healthcheck:
      # Keycloak 26.4 images ship no curl/wget; probe the management port (9000) over /dev/tcp.
      test: [ "CMD-SHELL", "bash -c 'exec 3<>/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/9000 && printf \"GET /health/ready HTTP/1.1\\r\\nHost: localhost\\r\\nConnection: close\\r\\n\\r\\n\" >&3 && timeout 3 head -1 <&3 | grep -q 200'" ]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 30
      start_period: 90s

  keycloak-db:
    image: gvenzl/oracle-xe:21-slim
    environment:
      ORACLE_PASSWORD: ${ORACLE_PASSWORD:-oracle-development-only}
      APP_USER: keycloak
      APP_USER_PASSWORD: ${KEYCLOAK_DB_PASSWORD:-keycloak-development-only}
    ports: [ "1521:1521" ]
    volumes: [ keycloak-oracle:/opt/oracle/oradata ]
    healthcheck:
      test: [ "CMD-SHELL", "healthcheck.sh" ]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 40
      start_period: 60s

  # Key-metadata DB (signing keys / rotation ops) — the only facade-owned DB.
  # Kept on a separate Oracle instance so key lifecycle is not coupled to Keycloak's DB.
  identity-meta-db:
    image: gvenzl/oracle-xe:21-slim
    environment:
      ORACLE_PASSWORD: ${ORACLE_PASSWORD:-oracle-development-only}
      APP_USER: identity_meta
      APP_USER_PASSWORD: ${IDENTITY_META_DB_PASSWORD:-identity-development-only}
    volumes: [ identity-meta-oracle:/opt/oracle/oradata ]
    healthcheck:
      test: [ "CMD-SHELL", "healthcheck.sh" ]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 40
      start_period: 60s

  vault:
    image: hashicorp/vault:1.20
    cap_add: [ IPC_LOCK ]
    environment:
      VAULT_DEV_ROOT_TOKEN_ID: ${VAULT_TOKEN:-root}
      VAULT_DEV_LISTEN_ADDRESS: "0.0.0.0:8200"
    ports: [ "8200:8200" ]
    healthcheck:
      # Dev server is plain HTTP — force VAULT_ADDR so `vault status` does not probe https.
      test: [ "CMD-SHELL", "VAULT_ADDR=http://127.0.0.1:8200 vault status || exit 1" ]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 10

  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    command: redis-server --appendonly yes
    volumes: [ identity-redis:/data ]
    healthcheck:

using Identity.Application.Scope;
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.Memory;

namespace Identity.Persistence.KeyManagement;

public sealed class EfScopeDefinitionLookup(KeyMetadataDbContext db, IMemoryCache cache) : IScopeDefinitionLookup, IScopeCacheInvalidator
{
    private const string ActiveKey = "scopes:active:v1";
    private const string RoleAllowedKey = "scopes:roleAllowed:v1";
    private static readonly TimeSpan Ttl = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5);

    public void Invalidate() { cache.Remove(ActiveKey); cache.Remove(RoleAllowedKey); }

    public async Task<bool> ExistsActiveAsync(string key, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        var active = await GetActiveAsync(ct);
        return active.Any(s => string.Equals(s.Key, key, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase));
    }

    public async Task<bool> IsScopeAllowedForRoleAsync(string role, string scopeKey, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        var map = await GetRoleMapAsync(ct);
        if (!map.TryGetValue(role, out var allowed)) return true;
        if (allowed.Count == 0) return true;
        return allowed.Contains(scopeKey);
    }

    private async Task<IReadOnlyCollection<ScopeDefinitionEntity>> GetActiveAsync(CancellationToken ct)
    {
        if (cache.TryGetValue(ActiveKey, out IReadOnlyCollection<ScopeDefinitionEntity>? c) && c is not null) return c;
        var list = await db.ScopeDefinitions.Where(s => s.IsActive).ToListAsync(ct);
        cache.Set(ActiveKey, (IReadOnlyCollection<ScopeDefinitionEntity>)list, Ttl);
        return list;
    }

    private async Task<Dictionary<string, HashSet<string>>> GetRoleMapAsync(CancellationToken ct)
    {
        if (cache.TryGetValue(RoleAllowedKey, out Dictionary<string, HashSet<string>>? c) && c is not null) return c;
        var rows = await (from ra in db.RoleAllowedScopes join s in db.ScopeDefinitions on ra.ScopeDefinitionId equals s.Id select new { ra.RoleName, s.Key }).ToListAsync(ct);
        var map = new Dictionary<string, HashSet<string>>(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase);
        foreach (var r in rows)
        {
            if (!map.TryGetValue(r.RoleName, out var set)) { set = new HashSet<string>(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase); map[r.RoleName] = set; }
            set.Add(r.Key);
        }
        cache.Set(RoleAllowedKey, map, Ttl);
        return map;
    }
}

public sealed class EfResourceScopeResolver(KeyMetadataDbContext db, IMemoryCache cache) : IResourceScopeResolver
{
    private const string Key = "scopes:resourceMap:v1";
    private static readonly TimeSpan Ttl = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5);
    public async Task<HashSet<string>> GetScopesForResourceAsync(string resourceKey, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        if (!cache.TryGetValue(Key, out Dictionary<string, HashSet<string>>? map) || map is null)
        {
            var rows = await (from m in db.ScopeResourceMappings
                              join s in db.ScopeDefinitions on m.ScopeDefinitionId equals s.Id
                              join r in db.ApplicationResources on m.ApplicationResourceId equals r.Id
                              select new { r.Key, ScopeKey = s.Key }).ToListAsync(ct);
            map = new Dictionary<string, HashSet<string>>(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase);
            foreach (var x in rows)
            {
                if (!map.TryGetValue(x.Key, out var set)) { set = new HashSet<string>(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase); map[x.Key] = set; }
                set.Add(x.ScopeKey);
            }
            cache.Set(Key, map, Ttl);
        }
        return map.TryGetValue(resourceKey, out var set2) ? set2 : new HashSet<string>(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase);
    }
}

public sealed class EfUserScopeStore(KeyMetadataDbContext db) : Identity.Application.Scope.IUserScopeReader, Identity.Application.Scope.IUserScopeWriter
{
    public async Task<Identity.Contracts.ScopedAccessDocument> GetAsync(string userId, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        var assigns = await db.UserRoleAssignments.Where(a => a.UserId == userId).ToListAsync(ct);
        if (assigns.Count == 0) return Identity.Contracts.ScopedAccessDocument.Empty;
        var ids = assigns.Select(a => a.Id).ToArray();
        var scopes = await db.AssignmentScopes.Where(s => ids.Contains(s.UserRoleAssignmentId)).ToListAsync(ct);
        var scopeIds = scopes.Select(s => s.Id).ToArray();
        var values = scopeIds.Length == 0 ? new List<AssignmentScopeValueEntity>()
            : await db.AssignmentScopeValues.Where(v => scopeIds.Contains(v.AssignmentScopeId)).ToListAsync(ct);
        var defMap = await db.ScopeDefinitions.ToDictionaryAsync(s => s.Id, s => s.Key, ct);
        var byAssign = new Dictionary<Guid, Dictionary<string, List<string>>>();
        foreach (var s in scopes)
        {
            if (!defMap.TryGetValue(s.ScopeDefinitionId, out var k)) continue;
            if (!byAssign.TryGetValue(s.UserRoleAssignmentId, out var d)) { d = new Dictionary<string, List<string>>(StringComparer.Ordinal); byAssign[s.UserRoleAssignmentId] = d; }
            d[k] = values.Where(v => v.AssignmentScopeId == s.Id).Select(v => v.Value).ToList();
        }
        var result = assigns.Select(a =>
        {
            byAssign.TryGetValue(a.Id, out var d);
            IReadOnlyDictionary<string, IReadOnlyCollection<string>> dict = d is null
                ? new Dictionary<string, IReadOnlyCollection<string>>(StringComparer.Ordinal)
                : d.ToDictionary(k => k.Key, v => (IReadOnlyCollection<string>)v.Value.ToArray(), StringComparer.Ordinal);
            return new Identity.Contracts.ScopedRoleAssignment(a.RoleName, dict);
        }).OrderBy(a => a.Role, StringComparer.Ordinal).ToArray();
        return new Identity.Contracts.ScopedAccessDocument(result);
    }

    public async Task<IReadOnlyDictionary<string, IReadOnlyCollection<string>>> GetEffectiveAsync(string userId, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        var doc = await GetAsync(userId, ct);
        var merged = new Dictionary<string, HashSet<string>>(StringComparer.Ordinal);
        foreach (var a in doc.Assignments) foreach (var kv in a.Scopes)
        {
            if (!merged.TryGetValue(kv.Key, out var set)) { set = new HashSet<string>(StringComparer.Ordinal); merged[kv.Key] = set; }
            foreach (var v in kv.Value) set.Add(v);
        }
        return merged.ToDictionary(k => k.Key, v => (IReadOnlyCollection<string>)v.Value.ToArray(), StringComparer.Ordinal);
    }

    public async Task SetAsync(string userId, IReadOnlyCollection<Identity.Contracts.ScopedRoleAssignmentDto> assignments, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        var existing = await db.UserRoleAssignments.Where(a => a.UserId == userId).ToListAsync(ct);
        var eIds = existing.Select(a => a.Id).ToArray();
        if (eIds.Length > 0)
        {
            var scs = await db.AssignmentScopes.Where(s => eIds.Contains(s.UserRoleAssignmentId)).ToListAsync(ct);
            var scIds = scs.Select(s => s.Id).ToArray();
            if (scIds.Length > 0)
            {
                var vals = await db.AssignmentScopeValues.Where(v => scIds.Contains(v.AssignmentScopeId)).ToListAsync(ct);
                db.AssignmentScopeValues.RemoveRange(vals);
            }
            db.AssignmentScopes.RemoveRange(scs);
            db.UserRoleAssignments.RemoveRange(existing);
            await db.SaveChangesAsync(ct);
        }
        if (assignments.Count == 0) return;
        var defs = await db.ScopeDefinitions.ToDictionaryAsync(s => s.Key, s => s.Id, StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase, ct);
        foreach (var a in assignments)
        {
            var ura = new UserRoleAssignmentEntity { Id = Guid.NewGuid(), UserId = userId, RoleName = a.Role.Trim(), AssignedAt = DateTimeOffset.UtcNow };
            db.UserRoleAssignments.Add(ura);
            foreach (var kv in a.Scopes)
            {
                if (!defs.TryGetValue(kv.Key, out var defId)) continue;
                var assignmentScope = new AssignmentScopeEntity { Id = Guid.NewGuid(), UserRoleAssignmentId = ura.Id, ScopeDefinitionId = defId };
                db.AssignmentScopes.Add(assignmentScope);
                foreach (var v in kv.Value.Distinct(StringComparer.Ordinal))
                    db.AssignmentScopeValues.Add(new AssignmentScopeValueEntity { Id = Guid.NewGuid(), AssignmentScopeId = assignmentScope.Id, Value = v.Trim() });
            }
        }
        await db.SaveChangesAsync(ct);
    }
}

        cache.Set(RoleAllowedKey, map, Ttl);
        return map;
    }
}

public sealed class EfResourceScopeResolver(KeyMetadataDbContext db, IMemoryCache cache) : IResourceScopeResolver
{
    private const string Key = "scopes:resourceMap:v1";
    private static readonly TimeSpan Ttl = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5);
    public async Task<HashSet<string>> GetScopesForResourceAsync(string resourceKey, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        if (!cache.TryGetValue(Key, out Dictionary<string, HashSet<string>>? map) || map is null)
        {
            var rows = await (from m in db.ScopeResourceMappings
                              join s in db.ScopeDefinitions on m.ScopeDefinitionId equals s.Id
                              join r in db.ApplicationResources on m.ApplicationResourceId equals r.Id
                              select new { r.Key, ScopeKey = s.Key }).ToListAsync(ct);
            map = new Dictionary<string, HashSet<string>>(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase);
            foreach (var x in rows)
            {
                if (!map.TryGetValue(x.Key, out var set)) { set = new HashSet<string>(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase); map[x.Key] = set; }
                set.Add(x.ScopeKey);
            }
            cache.Set(Key, map, Ttl);
        }
        return map.TryGetValue(resourceKey, out var set2) ? set2 : new HashSet<string>(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase);
    }
}

public sealed class EfUserScopeStore(KeyMetadataDbContext db) : Identity.Application.Scope.IUserScopeReader, Identity.Application.Scope.IUserScopeWriter
{
    public async Task<Identity.Contracts.ScopedAccessDocument> GetAsync(string userId, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        var assigns = await db.UserRoleAssignments.Where(a => a.UserId == userId).ToListAsync(ct);
        if (assigns.Count == 0) return Identity.Contracts.ScopedAccessDocument.Empty;
        var ids = assigns.Select(a => a.Id).ToArray();
        var scopes = await db.AssignmentScopes.Where(s => ids.Contains(s.UserRoleAssignmentId)).ToListAsync(ct);
        var scopeIds = scopes.Select(s => s.Id).ToArray();
        var values = scopeIds.Length == 0 ? new List<AssignmentScopeValueEntity>()
            : await db.AssignmentScopeValues.Where(v => scopeIds.Contains(v.AssignmentScopeId)).ToListAsync(ct);
        var defMap = await db.ScopeDefinitions.ToDictionaryAsync(s => s.Id, s => s.Key, ct);
        var byAssign = new Dictionary<Guid, Dictionary<string, List<string>>>();
        foreach (var s in scopes)
        {
            if (!defMap.TryGetValue(s.ScopeDefinitionId, out var k)) continue;
            if (!byAssign.TryGetValue(s.UserRoleAssignmentId, out var d)) { d = new Dictionary<string, List<string>>(StringComparer.Ordinal); byAssign[s.UserRoleAssignmentId] = d; }
            d[k] = values.Where(v => v.AssignmentScopeId == s.Id).Select(v => v.Value).ToList();
        }
        var result = assigns.Select(a =>
        {
            byAssign.TryGetValue(a.Id, out var d);
            IReadOnlyDictionary<string, IReadOnlyCollection<string>> dict = d is null
                ? new Dictionary<string, IReadOnlyCollection<string>>(StringComparer.Ordinal)
                : d.ToDictionary(k => k.Key, v => (IReadOnlyCollection<string>)v.Value.ToArray(), StringComparer.Ordinal);
            return new Identity.Contracts.ScopedRoleAssignment(a.RoleName, dict);
        }).OrderBy(a => a.Role, StringComparer.Ordinal).ToArray();
        return new Identity.Contracts.ScopedAccessDocument(result);
    }

    public async Task<IReadOnlyDictionary<string, IReadOnlyCollection<string>>> GetEffectiveAsync(string userId, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        var doc = await GetAsync(userId, ct);
        var merged = new Dictionary<string, HashSet<string>>(StringComparer.Ordinal);
        foreach (var a in doc.Assignments) foreach (var kv in a.Scopes)
        {
            if (!merged.TryGetValue(kv.Key, out var set)) { set = new HashSet<string>(StringComparer.Ordinal); merged[kv.Key] = set; }
            foreach (var v in kv.Value) set.Add(v);
        }
        return merged.ToDictionary(k => k.Key, v => (IReadOnlyCollection<string>)v.Value.ToArray(), StringComparer.Ordinal);
    }

    public async Task SetAsync(string userId, IReadOnlyCollection<Identity.Contracts.ScopedRoleAssignmentDto> assignments, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        var existing = await db.UserRoleAssignments.Where(a => a.UserId == userId).ToListAsync(ct);
        var eIds = existing.Select(a => a.Id).ToArray();
        if (eIds.Length > 0)
        {
            var scs = await db.AssignmentScopes.Where(s => eIds.Contains(s.UserRoleAssignmentId)).ToListAsync(ct);
            var scIds = scs.Select(s => s.Id).ToArray();
            if (scIds.Length > 0)
            {
                var vals = await db.AssignmentScopeValues.Where(v => scIds.Contains(v.AssignmentScopeId)).ToListAsync(ct);
                db.AssignmentScopeValues.RemoveRange(vals);
            }
            db.AssignmentScopes.RemoveRange(scs);
            db.UserRoleAssignments.RemoveRange(existing);
            await db.SaveChangesAsync(ct);
        }
        if (assignments.Count == 0) return;
        var defs = await db.ScopeDefinitions.ToDictionaryAsync(s => s.Key, s => s.Id, StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase, ct);
        foreach (var a in assignments)
        {
            var ura = new UserRoleAssignmentEntity { Id = Guid.NewGuid(), UserId = userId, RoleName = a.Role.Trim(), AssignedAt = DateTimeOffset.UtcNow };
            db.UserRoleAssignments.Add(ura);
            foreach (var kv in a.Scopes)
            {
                if (!defs.TryGetValue(kv.Key, out var defId)) continue;
                var assignmentScope = new AssignmentScopeEntity { Id = Guid.NewGuid(), UserRoleAssignmentId = ura.Id, ScopeDefinitionId = defId };
                db.AssignmentScopes.Add(assignmentScope);
                foreach (var v in kv.Value.Distinct(StringComparer.Ordinal))
                    db.AssignmentScopeValues.Add(new AssignmentScopeValueEntity { Id = Guid.NewGuid(), AssignmentScopeId = assignmentScope.Id, Value = v.Trim() });
            }
        }
        await db.SaveChangesAsync(ct);
    }
}
